summary: The console starts and fetches individual runs today (`POST /api/runs`, `GET /api/runs/{runId}`) but has no way to list what has already run, so a user who closes the tab loses their only route back to a report. This feature adds a paginated, status-filterable, most-recent-first listing endpoint (`GET /api/runs`) backed by a redesigned `RunStore` index, plus a server-rendered console page that shows id/status/start time/duration per run and links to each completed run's existing `/reports/` output — in-progress runs show as such with no report link. The store stays in-memory (no persistence across restart) and no change is made to how reports themselves are generated or served; the only new surface is the read/index path over runs the console already tracks.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: GET /api/runs returns previously recorded runs, most recent first
examples: 10 runs exist, started at times T1..T10; response order is T10, T9, ... T1

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The response is paged; a caller can request the next page without re-reading runs it has already seen, because the store grows for the lifetime of the process
examples: First request returns a page of N runs plus a cursor/token; a follow-up request with that cursor returns the next N runs with no overlap with the first page

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A caller can narrow the listing to a single status, so 'show me the failures' is one request
examples: GET /api/runs?status=failed returns only runs whose Status field is "failed"

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Asking for a page beyond the end returns an empty page, not an error
examples: A cursor pointing past the last run returns 200 OK with an empty runs array, not a 4xx

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The console has a page listing the runs — id, status, when it started, how long it took — where each row links to that run's report
A run still in progress is shown as such and has no report link
examples: A run with empty FinishedAt/ReportURL renders status "running" and the row has no anchor to /reports/...

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Someone using the keyboard alone can move through the list and open a report
The listing endpoint responds in under 200ms at p95 with 10,000 runs held in the store
Listing runs never blocks a run that is starting or finishing, and vice versa

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: GET /api/runs must respond within the stated latency budget even as the in-memory store grows to 10,000 runs

Reading the run list must not contend for the same lock/critical section as StartRun/CompleteRun in a way that serializes them — listing and run start/finish must proceed concurrently without blocking each other, independent of store size
The run history page must be fully operable via keyboard alone: tab order reaches every row's report link, focus state is visible, and no interactive element depends on a mouse/pointer event

Any change to how reports themselves are generated or served

boundedContext.owning: Console Run Management (apps/console/internal/runs + internal/httpserver run endpoints)
crossings: Static report serving (internal/httpserver's /reports/* file handler) — the new listing links out to existing report URLs but this feature does not modify report generation or serving, per the spec's explicit exclusion

readModels: RunHistoryPage — ordered (most-recent-first), cursor-paginated, optionally filtered by status

affectedComponents.reason: Current RunStore is a map[string]*Run behind one sync.RWMutex with no ordering or index — the direct blocker for most-recent-first ordering, cursor pagination, the p95<200ms/10k-runs NFR, and the non-blocking-reads-vs-writes NFR. Needs a maintained ordering index (e.g. an append-tracked slice/ring of run IDs updated on StartRun) plus a ListRuns(status, cursor, limit) method that reads that index rather than scanning/sorting the map per request.

Run struct already carries ID, Status, StartedAt, FinishedAt, ReportURL — sufficient for the listing page's id/status/started/duration/report-link columns and the in-progress (empty FinishedAt/ReportURL) case. No new fields expected; duration is derived, not stored.
Register the new GET /api/runs listing route and the new console page route (e.g. GET /runs) alongside the existing /api/runs family and the sole existing page route ('/').

Add a ListRuns API handler (status/cursor/limit query params, paged response) following the GetRun pattern, and a new page handler following the Root() pattern — this service renders HTML as a hand-written Go string with no templating engine, so the runs page follows that same convention rather than introducing a frontend framework.

Add a paged-response envelope (e.g. a RunsPage type with runs + next cursor) alongside the existing writeJSON/writeError helpers so the new endpoint follows this service's one existing response-shaping convention.
Extend with tests for GET /api/runs following the established httptest.Server pattern: ordering, pagination, status filter, empty-page-past-end, 10k-run performance, and concurrency-with-writes.

Only needs a change if RunStore's constructor signature changes to wire up the new ordering index; otherwise no change expected since runs.NewRunStore() and httpserver.New(reg, runStore) wiring stays the same shape.

dataModelChanges.description: In-memory RunStore needs an ordering index (e.g. an append-only slice of run IDs, or a doubly-linked structure) maintained alongside the existing map so runs can be listed most-recent-first and paged by a stable cursor without a full scan/sort per request. This is an internal Go data-structure change, not a database migration — no persistent schema exists, and the spec explicitly excludes persistence across restart.

apiChanges.change: New endpoint. Returns a paged, most-recent-first list of runs; accepts an optional status filter and a pagination cursor/limit; returns an empty page (200, empty array, no next cursor) when the cursor is past the end rather than an error.

New server-rendered HTML page listing runs (id, status, started-at, duration), each completed row linking to its /reports/... report URL; in-progress rows show status with no report link; fully keyboard-navigable.

architecturalFlags: RunStore's current concurrency model (single sync.RWMutex guarding one map) does not support ordered iteration or genuinely non-blocking reads-vs-writes at 10,000-run scale within a 200ms p95 budget — recommend architect review of the indexing/locking approach (e.g. an incrementally-maintained ordered index updated on write, a copy-on-write snapshot for reads, or sharding the lock) before implementation, since this choice will constrain every future run-store feature, not just this one.

Cursor design for pagination (opaque token vs. plain offset/limit) is a one-time structural decision the spec doesn't dictate — recommend pinning it down once via architect rather than letting the developer improvise it under this endpoint alone.

edgeCases.case: Cursor points past the end of the store
edgeCases.handling: Return an empty page (empty runs array, no next cursor) with 200 OK, not a 4xx error, per the spec

edgeCases.case: A run is still in progress (FinishedAt/ReportURL empty)
edgeCases.handling: Both the API response and the console page show status as running/in-progress with no report link and no completed duration

edgeCases.case: status filter value does not match any known run status
edgeCases.handling: Return an empty page rather than erroring, since the spec does not require status enum validation (see Open Questions)

edgeCases.case: ListRuns is called while StartRun or CompleteRun is in flight on another goroutine
edgeCases.handling: Listing must read a consistent snapshot of the ordering index without holding the store's write path open for the duration of the HTTP response
The ordering index must be maintained incrementally on write so a list request is O(page size), not O(store size), to hit the 200ms p95 budget

openQuestions: What is the default and maximum page size for GET /api/runs? The spec requires paging but doesn't set a number.

Should the pagination cursor be an opaque token or a plain offset/limit? The spec only requires that a caller can get the next page without re-reading what it already has — it doesn't mandate a scheme.
Should an unrecognized ?status= value return 400, or just an empty page (matching the empty-page-past-end precedent)?
For an in-progress run, does the page show elapsed time so far, or just a static 'running' label with no timer?

Does the runs page need to auto-refresh/poll for status changes, or is it a static snapshot per page load? The spec doesn't mention live updates, and 'listing runs never blocks a run that is starting or finishing' suggests polling load should be considered even if out of explicit scope.
